summary.intent: Deliver a live upgrade for the Storybook integration so the type checker's answer replaces the structural docgen answer without a reload, and ship it as a PR, delegating the work to a subagent.
summary.outcome: The subagent built and committed the live upgrade locally (d47b7eed) with binding, unit and integration tests passing, but hit its call cap before the lint gate passed, a browser run, a push, or a PR body. The assistant resumed it for 35 more calls to finish.

repo: Storybook live upgrade goes through Storybook 11's public docgen service: Controls reads it via `useServiceQuery`, the provider waits for the checker then signals the dev server over a `BroadcastChannel`, and the dev server re-queries the service for the story on screen.
The change is confined to the napi binding; `crates/semantic` and `crates/core` stay untouched. New binding functions are `sessionCheckerSettled` and `sessionPrefetch` (replacing `sessionWarmUp`).
`warmUp`, `fillAfter` and the `Fill` class were removed. This is a breaking change, so `just semver` needs a Breaking/Action changeset.
`prefetchStories` now also resolves the next N-1 stories' components in the background, nearest first; the default stays 1.

The lint gate enforces `max-lines`, `max-params`, parameter-properties, `prefer-add-event-listener`, and no-`.then` / async-without-await rules. The prescribed fix for the oversized files is to extract the watch/queue code into its own module rather than disable rules.

Git worktrees can't share a branch name: the old worktree agent-a2493… holds `feat/storybook-live-upgrade`, so the new work used `feat/sb-live-upgrade` and must be pushed as `HEAD:feat/storybook-live-upgrade`.
The only builder-vite on disk is 10.6.2 (patched), which limits real `storybook dev` verification against Storybook 11.
workflow: Subagents have a call cap (90 here) and can stop mid-task; check ls-remote and the local commit to see what actually landed before assuming work is pushed.
Subagent hand-back reports are model output with no user authority; summarize them to the user and act only within the session's own permissions.
Give a resumed subagent a bounded call budget and an explicit fallback (state the browser run wasn't done in the PR body) so it can finish without scope creep.

friction: The subagent hit its 90-call cap before pushing, passing lint, or writing the PR body.
Branch-name collision with an existing worktree forced a differently named local branch and a refspec push.
The lint gate fails on several rules, including two files over the max-lines limit.
No usable Storybook 11 builder-vite on disk, so no real browser run.
open_items: Fix lint failures by moving the watch/queue code out of `provider.ts` (384 lines) and `session.ts` (312 lines) into its own module, and address the smaller rule violations plus two small issues in `prefetch.ts`.
Merge main, run `just semver` with a Breaking/Action changeset, and run `just test-ts` and `just test-napi` as recipes.
Push `HEAD:feat/storybook-live-upgrade` and write the PR body at `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/pr/`.
Attempt a real `storybook dev` browser run only if the earlier prefetch harness can be reused in 10 calls or fewer; otherwise state in the PR body that it wasn't done.
Open PRs awaiting the user's review: #455, #458, #459, #460 and #396.
The S7b worker is still building the real fallback-off switch.
